assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength lattice proposal and on Ye's demonstration of record accuracy and stability with strontium, have redefined precision measurement. They reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and underpin tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and plans for a redefinition of the second. The physics (narrow clock transitions, controlled lattice light shifts, many-atom interrogation) is clear, original and of lasting consequence for atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: The credited pair is natural: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength concept and made the first lattice clock demonstrations, while Ye drove the accuracy and stability frontier and the many-body and quantum-engineered clock work. Other contributors (single-ion clock groups, Hall and Hansch on combs, already recognised in 2005) are separate achievements, so a two-person prize looks fair.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: multiple independent labs worldwide operate lattice clocks beyond the caesium standard and clock comparisons are routine. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would view the ion-clock and lattice-clock communities as needing joint recognition (for example Wineland's 2012 prize covered ion control) is not settled by the supplied text.
I am relying on my own knowledge of the history of the magic-wavelength proposal and have not independently verified priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells, opened a whole class of topological band phases. The idea is original, conceptually clean and has changed how band structure and surface states are understood across solid-state physics, with spillover into photonics and cold atoms.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step (Z2 classification, quantum spin Hall in graphene); Molenkamp's group demonstrated the effect experimentally in HgTe wells. Hasan's ARPES work on Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal are important but would crowd out a three-person limit. The competing entry B008 swaps Eugene Mele for Qi-Kun Xue, which concerns a related but distinct discovery, the quantum anomalous Hall effect.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent experiments in many materials confirm the topological classification and its surface states over roughly fifteen years, and the field is stable.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu-Kane-Mele three-dimensional work and ARPES verification (Hasan) is contested.
Practical applications are still limited, which may temper urgency.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard models with tunable parameters and, with quantum gas microscopes, single-site resolution. The Mott insulator transition and later fermionic Hubbard physics gave a controlled quantum simulator for many-body physics. As an atomic physicist I regard this as a field-defining accomplishment with a clear conceptual identity.
assessment.attribution: Experimental leadership is clear in Bloch, Greiner (Mott insulator in lattices, microscopy) and Esslinger (fermions in lattices, Fermi-Hubbard). Cirac and Zoller are credited as theorists proposing the quantum simulation concept, and Zoller and Jaksch-type proposals are not in the credited list, so a three-experimentalist configuration is defensible but leaves the theory origin of the Bose-Hubbard proposal unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature in its experimental core: many groups reproduce lattice quantum simulation, though the claim of simulation beating classical computation on open problems is still developing.
uncertainties: Tension between recognising experimentalists and the Jaksch-Zoller theory proposal under the Nobel three-person limit.
Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and the 2012 prize on quantum control of single particles could be argued either way.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED reproduces cavity QED with superconducting artificial atoms coupled to microwave resonators, reaching strong coupling and enabling dispersive readout and gates for superconducting qubits. It is original, conceptually transparent and it underpins today's superconducting quantum processors.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf (with Girvin and Huang, whose names are not on the credited list) contributed the theory proposal and first strong-coupling experiments. The three credited names form a coherent set; the absence of Girvin from the credited strings is a gap I cannot repair.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent groups. Recent recognition of macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits in 2025 makes the timing question delicate, since a related prize was just awarded.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits may argue for waiting.
Whether Schoelkopf's contributions outweigh Devoret's or others' is a matter of attribution I cannot settle from the supplied data.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene and their experimental realisation, with correlated insulators and superconductivity, opened the field of moire quantum materials. It is an original, tunable platform for strongly correlated physics with large subsequent impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald provided the decisive theory of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the key correlated-insulator and superconductivity discovery. Eva Andrei's early STM and transport work on twisted layers is also important and is outside a three-person group in my selection.
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced in many laboratories, but the field is under fifteen years old and the nature of the superconducting state is still unresolved, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the discovery mature enough, given open questions about pairing mechanism.
Credit competition with Andrei and with earlier theoretical work on twisted layers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measuring the third neutrino mixing angle theta13 at a surprisingly large value was a decisive result that made leptonic CP-violation searches feasible. The measurement is clear, precise and has lasting importance for neutrino physics.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K all contributed. The credited names (Luk and Wang for Daya Bay, Nishikawa for T2K) leave out RENO and Double Chooz leaders, so any three-person configuration is partly arbitrary and Nobel-style collaboration credit is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature: reactor and accelerator results agree and the angle is measured to a few percent.
uncertainties: Fairness of credit among several experimental collaborations.
Neutrino oscillations were recognised in 2015, so the incremental novelty may be argued.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-gain X-ray free-electron lasers based on self-amplified spontaneous emission give femtosecond, coherent, intense X-ray pulses that have transformed structural dynamics, chemistry and atomic physics, including inner-shell and attosecond-adjacent studies relevant to my own field. The conceptual basis is original and the instrument impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini and Kim are central for the high-gain SASE theory and FEL design; the experimental realisation at LCLS (Emma) and FLASH/European XFEL (Rossbach and colleagues) was a large team effort. Choosing two names is a defensible but incomplete representation.
assessment.maturity: Mature: several facilities operate worldwide and deliver a large body of science.
uncertainties: Whether this reads as a physics discovery versus a technology achievement and how the committee weighs accelerator physics.
Allocation between theorists, machine builders and the facility teams is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller's proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realisation by ion-trap groups launched ion-based quantum computing and simulation. It shows high-fidelity operations and has been a leading platform for quantum technologies.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the theorists of the 1995 proposal; Blatt is a leading experimentalist, with others such as Wineland and Monroe also central. Wineland's 2012 prize already recognised manipulation of individual quantum systems, which complicates a new allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature technologically, though large-scale quantum computing is still developing and some claims depend on progress still being made.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and the question of whether the trapped-ion contributions are separate enough.
Same theorists also appear in B037, which could split the credit.
